text:
Ten seasons after Vancouver drafted him, Michael DiPietro is the story in Boston. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis traced his long road back this week, and the numbers explain why people are writing about it: 4.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, a 4-1-0 run, .924 against hard shots.

The Bruins are 12-4-1 and project to about 101 points with a 79% playoff chance. Their goal difference is huge, 63-40. Their share of the chances is not: 50.71% of the expected goals (the quality of chances both ways). They've allowed 12.6 fewer goals than the shots deserved and scored 8.88 more, and our luck measure has them six points ahead of where the play says they'd be.

There is real stuff underneath. Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy have taken 63% of the expected goals together, 12-3 in goals. The rookie James Hagens line with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt has been the steadiest forward group at 55%.

Coming off a 6-2 win in Pittsburgh, they are fine for now. The test is what happens on the nights the goaltending is merely normal.
headline: DiPietro has the Bruins on top
